subject: How to get quantiles of the function of hyperparameter?

messages.author: 551aded02f98012e
messages.subject: How to get quantiles of the function of hyperparameter?
parts:
Hi all,
   I am very new to INLA,I tried a simulation and I want to get different quantile of the m.sig2 which is the exp(-tau.nu)(tau.nu is the hyperparameter of the m
#simulate data
set.seed(1)
N = 300 # reduced so could run example quickly
x = rnorm(N, mean = 3,sd = 1) 
nu = rnorm(N,0,2)
eta = exp(1 + 2*x + nu)
y = rpois(N,eta)
dat_INLA = data.frame(y,x,nu = 1:N)

#INLA call

library(INLA)
result = inla(formula = y~x+f(nu,model = "iid"),family = "poisson",data = dat_INLA,control.predictor = list(link = 1))

#compute different quantiles of sig2

#I don't know how to transform tau.nu_quant into sig2_quant
#tau.nu_quant = inla.qmarginal(c(0.025,0.5,0.975),result$marginals.hyperpar[[1]])
#so I do code following instead.
m.sig2 = inla.tmarginal(fun = function(x) exp(-x),
                        marginal = result$internal.marginals.hyperpar$`Log precision for nu`)
sig2_quant = quantile(m.sig2, probs <- c(0.025,0.5,0.975))

 
I don't know whether it is right.And according to the output,the mean of sig2_quant is about 2.2 which is not match with the var(nu)=4.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to get quantiles of the function of hyperparameter?
parts:
modified code is attached.

quantiles transforms directly: so when

sig2 = exp(-log.tau)

then the quantiles use the same transformation (here, in the reversed
order: see the code)

H
